chunks: And as for what was narrated: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hammad ibn Isa and Khalaf ibn Rabi', from al-Fadl, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had a female slave whom he had sexual relations with, and she died, and then he marries her daughter afterwards. He said: 'There is no harm; she is not in the same status as a free woman.'

Therefore, this report does not mention the permissibility of sexual intercourse; rather, it implies that he is permitted to marry her. We permit him to marry her afterwards provided he owns her. The prohibited aspect is her sexual intercourse (consumption), and this is not mentioned in the report.
And that which also indicates that the ruling for the free woman and the slave woman is the same is what was narrated:

key_terms.يَطَؤُهَا: He has sexual intercourse with her

ai.seo_question: Can a man marry the daughter of his female slave after she dies?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi cites this report to clarify that the Imam’s statement 'she is not in the status of a free woman' refers specifically to the prohibition of direct sexual intercourse (waṭʾ) with the slave, rather than invalidating the marriage contract (nikāḥ) with her daughter. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic principle that while a master may not directly enjoy his slave, he retains the right to marry her daughter, a ruling supported by the parallel permissibility of marrying free women.
